headline_status_explanation: After the Phase 0 / Tier-1.9 refactor, A1 and the four per-contract A3 sub-axioms (solidityVerifier / solidityWallet / solidityFactory / solidityMultiOwnable _compiles_correctly) are `opaque + axiom-equality` shapes carrying real propositional content. Removing any one would leave the per-claim corollaries unprovable. A2 (entrypoint_honest) and A4 (evm_bytecode_executes_correctly) remain cited-TCB per user decision. A5 (EUF-CMA + 3 hardness shape axioms) remain cited-TCB per Barbosa et al. 2024. The Lean kernel built-ins (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) are kernel-TCB. All three security claims are mathematically proven at the Lean kernel level, modulo the cited TCB axioms; theft_free's axiom closure is exactly {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, evm_bytecode_executes_correctly, precompile_0x02_is_FIPS_180_4, solidityVerifier_compiles_correctly, EUF_CMA_SPHINCSplusC, ITSR_F, SM_DT_TCR_F, hMsg_random_oracle, entrypoint_honest} (11), zero `sorry`, zero `True := trivial` theorem placeholders. UPDATE 2026-06-10: (a) the Lean verifier spec was made faithful to the deployed Yul's FORS hypertree-position binding (commit fcee705a) — `htIdx` is now folded into every FORS ADRS in `Spec/Adrs.lean` + `Spec/Fors.lean`; `verifyRefined_eq_spec` stays `rfl`. (b) The deployed `PQSmartWallet` was fixed so `bootstrapUses` is bumped in the validation phase (closing the PQBootstrapCapEvasion few-time under-count); the Lean model already encoded this. (c) Four `True := trivial` placeholders (no_reset_path; the three Verifier section lemmas) were upgraded to real theorems. (d) The Lean `validateSignature` model + `Factory.createAccountPrecondition` were made faithful to the deployed bytecode's ABI tail-pad check, audit-H-3 ownerIndex parity, and the install-time N-mask + duplicate-owner gates (previously the model accepted inputs the bytecode rejects). (e) A3.2/A3.3 were RE-RUN and DISCHARGED on the deployed bytecode (patched Halmos + z3, solver now available): A3.2 by a full POINTWISE-EQUIVALENCE session (`HalmosValidateUserOpEquiv` — deployed `validateUserOp` bytecode == the clause-for-clause Lean-model transcription `LeanValidateUserOpModel.sol`, over a symbolic envelope, under a generic uninterpreted verifier, conditioned on the kernel-proven reachable-state invariant) plus the per-property `HalmosValidateUserOp`/`HalmosExecute` rules; A3.3 by the `HalmosFactory` iff + reject rules. A3.2's axiom statement was tightened to carry the reachable-state hypothesis (the bytecode reverts on checked-arith overflow where the ℕ model returns failure — a divergence on UNREACHABLE states only). The bytecode-transported Lean corollaries `theft_free_bytecode` (closure += solidityWallet_compiles_correctly) and `factory_squat_defence_bytecode` (closure = solidityFactory_compiles_correctly + kernel) make the wallet/factory bridge axioms explicit in a `#print axioms`. The codehash pins are now profile-aware (default runs=200 AND deploy runs=999999), both certified, plus an immutable-window lemma (`PinnedBytecodeImmutableLemma`) transporting the per-instance pin to all instances modulo the two certified immutables. Reproduce: `make -C contracts/verification verify-bytecode`.

discharge_states.placeholder: Lean type reduces to `True` — axiom has no semantic content. Hostile removal would not break the proof.
discharge_states.misleading: Axiom has real content but states a property of a Lean model not formally connected to the deployed bytecode.
discharge_states.cited-tcb: Axiom has real content; discharge is a citation to a peer-reviewed proof or universally-trusted Ethereum infrastructure.
discharge_states.discharged-bytecode: Axiom has real content; a Halmos session, Certora rule-set, or differential test discharges it against pinned codehashes.
discharge_states.discharged-corollary: Axiom is a named corollary of another axiom that's already discharged or cited.
discharge_states.kernel-tcb: Lean 4 kernel built-in. Trusted as part of the kernel's soundness.

axioms.name: SphincsCVerify.Bridge.solidityVerifier_compiles_correctly
axioms.description: Deployed SPHINCsC10Asm.verify equals the Lean Yul model `verifyYulModel`.
axioms.lean_type: ∀ pkSeed pkRoot message sig, DeployedBytecode.SPHINCsC10Asm_verify ... = verifyYulModel ...
axioms.status_detail: Opaque-equality shape (load-bearing). Discharged in THREE layers. (1) Spec refinement: the Lean `Verifier/Equivalence.lean::verifyRefined_eq_spec` (rfl) ties the byte-offset verifier to the structural spec, INCLUDING the FORS hypertree-position binding (commit fcee705a: `htIdx` folded into every FORS ADRS via `Spec/Adrs.lean::forsNode/forsRoots` + `Spec/Fors.lean`), so the spec matches the deployed Yul byte-for-byte on that dimension. (2) Differential: 10 KAT vectors verify Rust ↔ Solidity bytecode ↔ Lean spec (`test/SPHINCsC10Asm.t.sol::test_verifyAllKatVectors`, PASS). (3) Bytecode symbolic gates: Halmos proves the verifier's INPUT-VALIDATION gates on the deployed bytecode (codehash 0xf1ef…fef5) for ALL inputs — wrong sig length reverts, non-N-masked pkSeed/pkRoot return false (`test/halmos/HalmosVerifier.t.sol`, 3 rules PASS). The verifier's FULL functional behaviour (FORS/WOTS/Merkle/hypertree over a 4008-byte sig, thousands of staticcall(0x02)) is NOT symbolically tractable and is intentionally left to layers (1)+(2); hence `discharged-bytecode-partial`. SHA-256 is uninterpreted throughout (= A1). Reproduce: `make -C contracts/verification verify-bytecode`.

discharge_artifacts.evidence: 3 rules PASS — input-validation gates only (length revert, N-mask reject); full functional equivalence left to the Lean refinement + KAT differential
verifyRefined_eq_spec (rfl) incl. FORS htIdx ADRS binding
Rust reference signer + Solidity verifier + Lean spec differential on the 10 shared KAT vectors (test_verifyAllKatVectors)

≈250-mutant wrong-accept battery on the deployed verifier bytecode (dense single-bit/single-byte flips across all structural regions, whole-region zeroing, degenerate sigs, key/message perturbation) — every near-miss REJECTED; positive control (valid vector accepted) prevents a vacuous pass. Empirical (finite battery), the negative-direction complement of the KAT positive direction; the full ∀-signature equivalence stays on the Lean refinement = why A3.1 is -partial.

axioms.description: Deployed PQSmartWallet.validateUserOp equals the Lean validateSignature model.
axioms.lean_type: ∀ s op ep cid, (∀ i, s.slotUses i + s.offchainSigCount i ≤ MaxSlotUses) → DeployedBytecode.PQSmartWallet_validateUserOp ... = validateSignature ... DeployedBytecode.SPHINCsC10Asm_verify
axioms.status_detail: DISCHARGED 2026-06-10 by Halmos symbolic execution of the deployed PQSmartWallet runtime bytecode (codehash 0x43c654…a06a default profile / 0x551c4e…default-vs-deploy both pinned + certified by test/PinnedCodehashes.t.sol in the same flow). PRIMARY artifact: a full POINTWISE-EQUIVALENCE session (test/halmos/HalmosValidateUserOpEquiv.t.sol, 3 rules PASS) proving the deployed `validateUserOp` bytecode returns the SAME (result, post-storage) as the clause-for-clause Lean-model transcription `test/halmos/LeanValidateUserOpModel.sol` — over a symbolic envelope (every byte of the 4128-byte wrapper symbolic; callData/initCode/paymasterAndData swept over length classes with symbolic content; all scalar fields symbolic; counters symbolic under the reachable-state invariant; owners symbolic) and under a GENERIC input-dependent uninterpreted verifier (OracleSPHINCSVerifier — binds the verifier's argument bytes, strictly more general than instantiating the deployed verifier), plus a reverting-verifier arm. This is the axiom's exact equality, not selected corollaries. SUPPORTING: the per-property rules (HalmosValidateUserOp.t.sol 8 — non-bypass over a SYMBOLIC verifier result = Lean I-1, validation-phase cap bump = the PQBootstrapCapEvasion fix, role-split, widened tail-pad, EntryPoint-only; HalmosExecute.t.sol 6 — execute gated by a prior verifier-true validate, one-shot, self-target rejected single+batch). The axiom carries a REACHABLE-STATE HYPOTHESIS (combined cap ≤ MaxSlotUses): outside it the bytecode reverts on Solidity-0.8 checked-add overflow where the ℕ model returns failure — a divergence on UNREACHABLE states (the kernel-proven `combinedCap_inductive` establishes the hypothesis at init and preserves it); stating the unconditional ∀ would be FALSE. SHA-256 stays an uninterpreted function throughout (bottoms out at A1). The Lean model `Wallet/ValidateUserOp.lean::validateSignature` is the kernel-checked source, and `Spec/Theorems.lean::theft_free_bytecode` transports theft-freedom onto the opaque deployed-bytecode symbol via this axiom. Reproduce: `make -C contracts/verification verify-bytecode`. TCB note: Halmos output is a cited solver session (Halmos+z3 soundness + harness↔property match + the transcription LeanValidateUserOpModel↔Lean which is a side-by-side syntactic correspondence), not a Lean proof term; recorded under contracts/verification/halmos/sessions/.

axioms.status_detail: DISCHARGED 2026-06-10 by Halmos symbolic execution of the deployed factory runtime bytecode (codehash 0xfa2922…7c3c, certified by test/PinnedCodehashes.t.sol). 5 rules PASS over all inputs (test/halmos/HalmosFactory.t.sol): the BICONDITIONAL `createAccount` succeeds ⟺ the Lean `Factory.createAccountPrecondition` holds (verifier accepts over `addSlot0Digest` with the verifier result symbolic, i.e. proven for EVERY verifier answer, AND right chain), over symbolic chainId + symbolic signature, with the success arm additionally proving the deploy postconditions (predicted CREATE2 address, both owner-byte installs, owner count); plus the already-deployed top-up early-return (returns the existing wallet unmodified ⟺ right chain) and three reject rules witnessing the precondition's install-gate conjuncts (non-N-masked master, non-N-masked slot-0, duplicate slot-0). The Lean precondition was extended 2026-06-10 with these N-mask + distinct conjuncts to match the deployed `initialize → _addOwnerAtIndex` gates. Keys are concrete in the iff (a symbolic owner half makes Halmos havoc the proxy storage on the phantom already-deployed CREATE2 fork) while chainId+signature stay symbolic; the gate conjuncts are each covered by a concrete reject rule. The run exercises the genuine factory path (sha256 salt+digest, CREATE2 proxy deploy, initialize). SHA-256 uninterpreted (= A1). `factory_squat_defence_bytecode` (Spec/Theorems.lean) transports I-8 onto the opaque deployed-bytecode symbol via this axiom. Reproduce: `make -C contracts/verification verify-bytecode`. The prior Certora rule-set remains an alternative discharge path.

headline_one_line: All three security claims (signature-to-execution binding, owner-set integrity, execution faithfulness) are mathematically proven at the Lean kernel level. A3.2 (wallet) is DISCHARGED on the deployed bytecode by a full POINTWISE-EQUIVALENCE Halmos session against the clause-for-clause Lean-model transcription (over a symbolic envelope, generic uninterpreted verifier, conditioned on the kernel-proven reachable-state invariant) plus 14 per-property rules; A3.3 (factory) by the createAccount⟺precondition iff + reject rules — both against the profile-aware pinned codehashes (certified by PinnedCodehashes.t.sol + the immutable-window lemma). A3.1 (verifier) is discharged-bytecode-partial — Halmos input gates + Lean refinement (incl. FORS htIdx binding) + 10 KAT vectors + a ≈250-mutant adversarial wrong-accept screen on the bytecode; the full ∀-signature functional equivalence is the named -partial gap. A1 (SHA-256) stays uninterpreted in every Halmos run (the named boundary). A2 (EntryPoint), A4 (EVM), and A5 (EUF-CMA) remain cited-TCB per user decision. The Lean corollaries theft_free_bytecode / factory_squat_defence_bytecode quantify theft-freedom + squat-defence directly over the opaque deployed-bytecode symbols.
